assessments.reasoning: I independently retrieved and verified the exact bytes of Introduction to the 'RS' Portable Algol 68 Compiler and inspected the cited passage (Summary and §§1–2, printed pp. 1–3 (physical PDF pp. 4–6)). TN802 §2 on printed page 3 expressly names Revised Report ALGOL 68 as the language accepted by the compiler and itemizes deviations and extensions. Its Summary and §1 identify the portable compiler.

challenge.method: Read the mode and identifier declaration-order change, representation differences and vector extension, then compare the 1978 compiler manual §1.1.
challenge.results: Both documents establish the Revised Report base with deviations. This supports an implementation relationship with the documented accepted-language qualification.

limitations: TN802 itself describes its contents as preliminary to definitive system or accepted-language documentation. The verdict remains source-attributed.
